newsitem.title: USA: CME live, feeder cattle end mostly lower.
newsitem.headline: CME live, feeder cattle end mostly lower.

text.p: CME live and feeder cattle futures closed mostly lower with live cattle pressured by packers' reluctance to raise bids for cash cattle, traders said.
Feeder cattle closed mostly lower, pressured by the decline in deferred live cattle futures. However, November ended higher, buoyed late by a steep drop in CBOT corn futures.

Negative operating margins discouraged meat packers from actively paying $71.00 per cwt for feedlot cattle, traders said. There were a few $71.00 sales Wednesday, but $70.00 was the top price paid Thursday in light volume.
"I don't think they are going to (actively) pay $71.00. The packers are losing money," said one trader early in the session.

Selling in December live cattle increased after the October expired. October's premium to December supported the latter contract until expiration. October expired at 1200 CDT at 73.00 cents per lb versus December's close at 65.800.
Feeder cattle futures closed mostly lower after a session of light trading. November closed with a thin gain, the result of a late sharp drop in CBOT corn futures.
Other feeder cattle contracts traded in a narrow range on both sides of unchanged.

Live cattle closed up 0.225 cent a lb to down 0.225 cent with October up 0.225 at 73.000 cents and December was off 0.150 at 65.800. Feeder cattle were up 0.050 to off 0.200 cent a lb with October off 0.075 at 63.050 cents and November up 0.050 at 63.575.
